text:
anya: Quick follow-up from the RFC — we keep hitting edgecases where hosted/dedicated/private have diverged behaviours for routing and secrets. wanna sync before the next sprint.
ryan: +1, saw a prod alert last week where private fallthrough picked the wrong model variant.
samir: Can you paste the alert? trying to connect dots with the manifest change.
anya: logs were noisy, but core issue was the controlplane translating `model_hint` -> variant id differently for VPCs.
anya: Example diff:```json
// hosted request
{
  "model": "rw-large",
  "mode": "hosted",
  "hint": "latency-optim"
}
// private request after translation
{
  "model": "rw-large-v2-quant",
  "mode": "private",
  "hint": "latency-optim"
}
```
lucy: that translation is done by the private adapter, right? it applies a quant profile by default.
ryan: yes — adapter applies default quant/profiles unless controlplane confirms capability. fallback uses `compat-mode=true`.
samir: problem: compat-mode was assumed safe, but v2-quant changes tokenization slightly (edgecase outputs). customers saw hallucinations in structured outputs.
anya: so we need binding-level guarantees: adapter can change performance knobs, but must preserve output shape + tokenization unless explicitly requested.
ryan: options: 1) require adapter to advertise `preserves-tokenization:true` in capability manifest, 2) make controlplane do a light probe on new variants (sample prompts) before routing live traffic, 3) add a canary route for variant rollouts.
lucy: 3 is already used for model versioning, but not for hosting-mode transitions — probably worth extending.
samir: tradeoffs: probe adds latency to deployment, canary adds traffic routing complexity, manifest flag relies on adapter honesty.
anya: recommended short-term: require a manifest flag + automatic canary config when mode translation would switch quantization or tokenizer.
ryan: +1, and add a devex warning in Console when adapters without flag exist.
infra-bot: reminder: there is an existing feature-flag `adapter-safety-probes` in staging. enable-by-default for next week?
lucy: enable in staging. we should run a small corpus of evals (10 prompts) during probe.
samir: also need audit logs showing pre/post translation mapping and the probe results. ops needs that for rollback decisions.
anya: agree. I suggest an action list: 1) spec manifest field `preserves_tokenization` (samir), 2) implement canary routing for hosting-mode variant translation (ryan), 3) enable staging probe + eval corpus (lucy), 4) add audit events for translation & probe (infra team).
ryan: timeline? I can stub canary changes this sprint but need a followup for traffic steering edgecases.
samir: i can draft the manifest schema today, include examples and deprecation notes.
lucy: I'll pick a 10-prompt eval set with representative structured outputs: JSON tables, code blocks, short Q&A.
anya: Cool — pair up for implementation reviews. Also: add a note to run the probe against quantized variants in dedicated before enabling in private.
ryan: will do.
infra-bot: deploybot: canary toggle created: `canary.adapter-mode-translation` set to off in prod, on in staging.
anya: Thanks. one more UX ask — Console should label a route as "mode-translated" when translation occurred so engineers can filter traces.
lucy: UI epic filed: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2042 : will link once spec is in.
samir: ok moving forward with manifest PR, ping me for review.
anya: Great thread. We'll regroup after the manifest PR lands. :thumbsup:
